newsitem.title: UK: UK's Kingfisher rides high in 3rd qtr.
newsitem.headline: UK's Kingfisher rides high in 3rd qtr.

text.p: Retail group Kingfisher Plc benefited from higher consumer spending when it reported third quarter results on Wednesday showing a 7.5 percent hike in like-for-like sales.
The group, which owns popular UK retail chains Comet, Woolworths and B&Q dealing in electrical goods to beauty products, had total sales growth of 12.9 percent to 1.345 billion stg ($2.2 billion).
In a statement, Kingfisher said B&Q, Comet and Woolworths all achieved double digit growth.
B&Q, the do-it-yourself home products chain, was the highest revenue earner with sales up 18.5 percent at 365.9 million stg.
"Its two formats -- supercentres and warehouses -- both achieved similar like-for-like increases," Kingfisher said.
Woolworths sales for the same period rose 13.2 percent to 324.3 million stg, mainly on gains made in the first half.
The targeted roll-out of new format local stores was completed and there were now 117. The new format is increasing sales on average by 22 percent.
Electrical goods retailer Comet had sales growth of 16.5 percent. The figures did not include the recently-acquired Norweb retail unit.
Darty, the group's French electricals division, increased sales by 2.3 percent at actual rates.
"At constant exchange rates, the sales increase was 2.0 percent after adjusting for sales made by the Belgian subsidiary New Vanden Borre."
Darty's like-for-like sales edged up only by 0.4 percent in difficult trading conditions.
Kingfisher's Superdrug division showed sales growth of 6.6 percent with like-for-like sales climbing 5.4 percent.
The groups's total sales for the 39-week period to November 2, 1996 stood at 3.85 billion stg, up 11.5 percent from its previous year's 3.46 billion.
--Arindam Nag, London Newsroom +44-171-542 7717 ($ = 0.608 British Pounds Sterling)
